questions.title: Main site of blood cell destruction
questions.question: Blood cell destruction occurs mainly in the:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The bone marrow is where blood cells are made, not where they are destroyed; production and destruction happen at different sites.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The kidneys filter plasma and regulate fluid and electrolyte balance; they are not the main site of blood cell removal.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The heart pumps blood around the circulation; it plays no role in removing aged blood cells from it.
explanations.D: Correct. The spleen is the main site of blood cell destruction. Aged, fragile red cells are squeezed through its narrow splenic cords and sinusoids, and macrophages lining the red pulp phagocytose those that can no longer deform enough to pass through, alongside worn platelets and other spent cells.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the spleen as the main site of blood cell destruction.

questions.title: Erythrocytes and blood viscosity
questions.question: About erythrocytes:

options.B: They are responsible for the major part of blood viscosity
options.C: Their life span is about 2 months
options.D: Their Hb content carries only O2

explanations.A: Incorrect. Erythrocytes do contain enzymes — carbonic anhydrase in particular, which speeds the interconversion of carbon dioxide and bicarbonate — so this blanket denial is false.
explanations.B: Correct. Erythrocytes are responsible for the major part of blood's viscosity. Whole blood is about three times as viscous as water while plasma alone is only about 1.5 times as viscous, and that extra viscosity comes overwhelmingly from the suspended red cells, which make up the great majority of blood's cellular volume.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The erythrocyte's life span is about four months (120 days), not two.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Haemoglobin carries more than oxygen alone — it also carries some carbon dioxide as carbamino-haemoglobin and buffers hydrogen ions — so "only O2" understates its function.

questions.learning_objective: State that erythrocytes account for the major part of blood's viscosity relative to plasma alone.

questions.title: Advantage of the biconcave erythrocyte shape
questions.question: The biconcave shape of erythrocytes has the following advantage:

options.A: Produces a smaller surface area than a spherical cell of the same volume
options.B: Allows erythrocytes to be squeezed through small capillaries without rupture
options.C: Results in high tension on the membrane when the volume of the cell changes
options.D: Allows a small surface area for gas exchange
options.E: It allows free diffusion of ions

explanations.A: Incorrect. Biconcavity does the opposite: for the same enclosed volume it gives a LARGER surface area than a sphere would, not a smaller one, which is part of why it helps gas exchange rather than limiting it.
explanations.B: Correct. The biconcave shape's key advantage is flexibility: it lets the erythrocyte fold and deform as it is squeezed through capillaries narrower than its own resting diameter, without its membrane rupturing. That reversible deformability is what lets the cell survive repeated passage through the microcirculation for its full lifespan.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The biconcave shape's slack membrane surface area actually minimises tension when the cell's volume changes, rather than producing high tension; that slack is part of the same flexibility this shape provides.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Biconcavity increases the surface area available for gas exchange relative to a sphere of the same volume, not reduces it.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Free ion diffusion is a property of the membrane's ion channels and transporters, not a consequence of the cell's overall biconcave shape.

questions.learning_objective: Explain that the biconcave shape's flexibility, not a reduced surface area, is what lets the erythrocyte pass through narrow capillaries without rupturing.

questions.title: Erythrocyte structure — the false statement
questions.question: About the structure of erythrocytes, which of the following is FALSE?

options.A: Are surrounded with plastic semipermeable membrane
options.B: Hemoglobin is the main constituent of the erythrocytes
options.C: K is the chief intracellular cation
options.D: It is a nucleated biconcave disc

explanations.A: Incorrect as the false statement. The erythrocyte membrane genuinely is an elastic ("plastic"), semipermeable lipid bilayer, consistent with the deformability the cell needs to cross narrow capillaries.
explanations.B: Incorrect as the false statement. Haemoglobin genuinely is the main constituent of the erythrocyte's cytoplasm, occupying most of its internal volume and giving the cell its oxygen-carrying function.
explanations.C: Incorrect as the false statement. Potassium genuinely is the chief intracellular cation of the erythrocyte, as it is for cells generally, maintained by the membrane's sodium-potassium pump.
explanations.D: Correct — this is the false statement. The mature erythrocyte is anucleated, not nucleated: it extrudes its nucleus during maturation before entering the circulation. Calling it a "nucleated biconcave disc" is false on the nucleated part even though the biconcave-disc shape itself is accurate. This nucleus-extrusion fact is one of the most repeatedly tested facts in this bank.
explanations.E: Incorrect as the false statement. The erythrocyte genuinely has no mitochondria, which is exactly why it depends on anaerobic glycolysis for its energy rather than oxidative phosphorylation.

questions.learning_objective: Identify "nucleated" as the false element in an otherwise accurate description of erythrocyte structure.

questions.title: Removal of old or damaged erythrocytes
questions.question: Old or damaged erythrocytes are removed from the blood by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Eosinophils are specialised against large parasites such as helminths; removing worn-out erythrocytes is not their role.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Lymphocytes mediate humoral and cell-mediated immunity; they are not phagocytic cells and do not remove aged red cells.
explanations.C: Correct. Macrophages, mainly in the spleen and to a lesser extent the liver and bone marrow, phagocytose old or damaged erythrocytes. They recognise red cells that have become too fragile or altered to keep circulating and remove them, recycling the iron and breaking down the haemoglobin into bilirubin.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Monocytes are the circulating precursor of tissue macrophages, but it is the differentiated tissue macrophage, not the circulating monocyte itself, that carries out red cell removal in the spleen.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Neutrophils are the first line of defence against bacteria; clearing senescent red cells is not their function.

questions.learning_objective: Identify macrophages as the cell type that removes old or damaged erythrocytes from the circulation.
